dedupe_keys.name: statistics canada incident based fire statistics national fire information database fires by type of incident and structure 2005 to 2021

description: This table counts the fires attended by Canadian fire services each year, broken down by the kind of incident and the type of structure involved, and is the national summary of the National Fire Information Database. It is published by Statistics Canada under its National Fire Information Database programme. Coverage is Canada and each province or territory from 2005 to 2021, with the last release in June 2023; the Canada total includes only reporting jurisdictions (Ontario, Manitoba, British Columbia, Nova Scotia and the Canadian Armed Forces for all years, with New Brunswick, Saskatchewan, Alberta and Yukon for parts of the period). Each row gives a year, a geography, a fire incident type and a structure type with the number of incidents, and cube metadata describe the dimensions. The whole table is available as a free download in CSV or SDMX form under the Statistics Canada Open Licence, and carries its own DOI. Caveats: the table has not been updated since 2023, Quebec and several provinces are absent, and casualties, losses and response times are not in this table. Simulation uses: setting fire incident rates by province and structure type in fire service demand and station coverage models, and comparing trends with other countries. Related records: US NFIRS (data-usfa-nfirs-public-data-release) is the incident-level US counterpart, and the Scottish fire statistics (data-sfrs-fire-stations-and-incident-statistics) provide another national series.
